hypothesis: Per the logit-adjustment/prior-correction literature (Menon et al. 2021, adapted to CTR as noted in the literature summary), add a fixed per-video popularity-prior offset τ·log(π_v/(1-π_v)) — where π_v is a train-only, Bayesian-shrunk video positive rate — to DeepFM's raw logit *only when computing the training loss/gradient*, and score with the unadjusted raw logit at inference. This forces the embeddings to encode signal beyond "this video is generally popular," which past feature-addition attempts at popularity signal (iter 3) failed to achieve because they gave the model an *extra input feature* rather than removing the popularity shortcut from the training gradient itself — a genuinely different mechanism (training-procedure/popularity_debiasing, not feature_addition).
reflection: Iter 5's research call surfaced a concrete, actionable technique (logit adjustment / prior correction) that I hadn't tried before and that directly targets the popularity-skew mechanism the EDA flagged (Gini=0.79) — this is different from the feature-addition and pairwise-loss mechanisms already rejected, so I'm implementing it now rather than spending my last research call re-asking a question that's already answered.
expected_effect: GAUC should improve more than nDCG@5, since GAUC is a per-user pairwise-ranking measure and this technique directly reshapes the training gradient to stop rewarding the model for merely reproducing item popularity, which should sharpen within-user relative ordering; nDCG@5 (dominated by whichever few items land in the top-5, where genuinely popular items are often still legitimately relevant) may move less or even dip slightly.
